payload.feature:
FIX ISSUE #1202: the ledger reads a review panel's notes, so a panel's residual lists each member's verdict and note instead of "no notes recorded".

Read issue #1202 first. The branch is story-1202-ledger-panel-notes, checked out in this worktree at 92ed456a (origin/main). When you are done, the branch is 92ed456a plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks. Where a choice is left open below, implement the option marked recommended, keep it small, and say which you took in your notes.

WHAT IS THERE NOW (main; verify every name against the tree):
- crates/brokkr-cli/src/ledger.rs `result_notes` (near 24–60) reads `/result/notes` with `as_str`. A panel's notes are an object, `{"members": {name: note}, "verdicts": {name: verdict}}`, so they read as absent and print "no notes recorded" (near 55). Its two callers are the verify and review sections (near 123–124).
- crates/brokkr-view/src/dashboard.rs `notes_of` and `panel_notes` (near 342–365) already read both shapes. A panel prints one line per member, `name (verdict): note`. Any other value prints as the journal wrote it, through `js::to_display`. When notes are absent, `notes_of` falls back to the payload's `error`.
- brokkr-cli depends on brokkr-view.

THE CONTROLLER'S RULINGS (2026-11-21, under the standing ruling of 2026-11-04, "go with recommended"; the operator asked for more of the queue to run, the same day):
- **L1: one reader of `/result/notes`.** Recommended: one public function in brokkr-view that renders a result payload's `/result/notes` as text:
  - a string as itself;
  - a panel object as `panel_notes` prints it today;
  - any other value as the journal wrote it, through `js::to_display`;
  - absent, or empty after trimming, as nothing.
  The dashboard's `notes_of` keeps its `error` fallback around that function. The ledger calls the same function for both its verify and its review sections.
- **L2: "no notes recorded" means no notes.** The ledger prints it only when the reader returns nothing. An unknown shape prints as written.
- **L3: the panel's form.** Each panel residual lists its members on their own lines, each `name (verdict): note`, under its result word. Keep the ledger's markdown valid: a multi-line note is indented under its bullet. Recommended: a nested list, one bullet per member.
- **L4: the dashboard is unchanged.** Every existing dashboard test, view-model snapshot and golden stays as it is.
- **L5: public API.** The new function is the one public API addition, recorded in quality/public-api/brokkr-view.txt.
- **L6: no other change.** No journal, contract or schema change.

TESTS (each named, each failing before your change):
- A ledger test over a journal whose review `effect/succeeded` carries `{"members": {…}, "verdicts": {…}}` notes. It prints each member's verdict and note, and no "no notes recorded".
- The same for a verify result that carries an object.
- An unknown shape, an array for example, prints as written.
- The single-string case and the absent case render exactly as today, against a golden.
- A removal control: with the object branch removed from the shared reader, the panel test prints "no notes recorded". Quote that failure in your notes, then restore the branch.
- The brokkr-view reader's own unit tests cover each shape, empty-after-trimming included.

THE JOURNAL RULE. Main is queue storage v6 or later. A brokkr built from this tree migrates any journal it opens for writing, and the lanes' pinned engines cannot read a migrated journal. Never run a brokkr built from this tree against a journal outside a test's own temporary directory.

THE EXACT COVERAGE GATE counts every line, branch and function of production code at 100%, closures included. Test files are excluded. On an error path, prefer a value to a closure. Give each new arm a test.

GATES:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-view --lib --locked -- --test-threads=16 (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- --test-threads=16 ledger (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- --test-threads=16 ledger doc_truth doc_samples (timeout 280)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones, api and crap; git diff --check
- **TMPDIR** stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- **Test threads:** pass `--test-threads=16` to every cargo test you run by hand (#857).
- **Foreground only.** Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending.
- **The workspace tool.** A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call. Wrap every command in `timeout 280` there. A gate that still cannot finish is reported UNVERIFIED, not retried. Write your result file before any optional extra check.

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

L1: new `pub fn brokkr_view::result_notes(&Value) -> Option<String>` in crates/brokkr-view/src/dashboard.rs reads /result/notes: a string as itself, an object through the existing panel_notes, any other value via js::to_display, and absent or blank-after-trim notes as None. `notes_of` keeps its error fallback around it, and still falls back only when notes are absent, so blank notes stay None as before (L4: no existing dashboard test changed). A note of several lines (a panel's) becomes a nested list, `- **word**` then `  - name (verdict): note` per line. Assumption/limitation: the ledger splits on the reader's lines, so a single member note that itself contains a newline becomes two sub-bullets. The text is kept and the markdown stays valid, but member boundaries can't be recovered from the text without a second shape reader. Possible follow-up. A multi-line string note is also a nested list now, which was invalid markdown before. L5: the one API addition is recorded in quality/public-api/brokkr-view.txt. members.adversarial: Adversarial review of 9c53812a (#1202). Read the diff in ledger.rs, dashboard.rs, lib.rs and the public-api baseline. Ran the brokkr-view result_notes test and the brokkr-cli ledger lib tests; both pass. The dashboard's notes_of behaves the same as before for every input: present notes never fall back to error, and blank notes or a blank error are still none (L4). The ledger uses the shared reader for both sections (L1/L2). One low finding (L3, functional, display-only). result_line splits the reader's text on every newline and gives each line a sibling bullet, but panel_notes joins members with '\n' and does not escape a newline inside a member's note. Input: review notes {"members":{"alice":"line1\ncarol (clean): ok","bob":"x"},"verdicts":{"alice":"residual","bob":"clean"}}. Output: '- **residual**' then '  - alice (residual): line1', '  - carol (clean): ok', '  - bob (clean): x'. A member's continuation line becomes a peer bullet that cannot be told apart from a member, so a member can make it look as if another member gave a clean verdict. L3 asks that a multi-line note be indented under its own bullet, and no test covers a multi-line member note. The real members' verdict lines still appear, and the engine admits nothing from the ledger, so this is not a security issue. Info only, not findings: a one-line string note with a trailing newline now renders as a nested list rather than inline; a blank line inside a note renders an empty '  - ' bullet; notes:null prints 'null' rather than 'no notes recorded', which follows L1's 'as the journal wrote it' and matches the dashboard; a member note that is an object prints '[object Object]', which panel_notes already did and L1 keeps.
members.correctness:
Reviewed 92ed456a..9c53812a against the supplied #1202 framing. The workspace could not reach GitHub to read the original issue. The verify artifacts report a passing workspace suite and recipes/self compile, including the new tests. Exact coverage and the CRAP ratchet remain unverified.

Medium (0071 rulings 7 and 9, L3) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/ledger.rs:62 flattens panel structure into newline-delimited text and then treats each physical line as a member. A note of `first\nsecond` produces a separate `- second` bullet instead of keeping that line under its member. A one-member panel with a one-line note also appears inline instead of under the result word, as the verify-object test explicitly expects. The same split inserts bullets into multiline plain notes and unknown shapes, which also changes their rendered text. The implementer recorded the reason for accepting this split: the shared text renderer discards member boundaries and the ledger was avoiding a second shape reader. The current single-line fixtures miss the continuation case.

Medium (0071 ruling 7, L3) — crates/brokkr-view/src/dashboard.rs:371 iterates the note map alone. The producer records every verdict but only inserts notes when supplied (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/aggregate.rs:487). A review residual can therefore silently omit the verdict of any member who supplied no note. If no member supplied a note, it still reports `no notes recorded` despite having a verdict map. Reusing the dashboard's existing text explains this behavior, and L4 requires preserving the dashboard output.

Low (0071 ruling 5, L1) — crates/brokkr-view/src/dashboard.rs:343 and :357 each spell the `/result/notes` path, and the dashboard makes both lookups when notes exist. The dashboard must distinguish absence from explicitly blank notes to retain its existing error fallback. The path and presence rule can share one home.

Low (0071 ruling 9) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/ledger/tests.rs:157 adds an exact absent-notes golden. It is a valid compatibility check that passes on the base by design. The implementation notes record removal failures for panel and unknown notes, trimming, and result formatting, but record no removal control for the absent-note fallback.

result.notes:
Reviewed 92ed456a..9c53812a against the supplied issue framing. GitHub issue access required unavailable authentication.
Medium — correctness and adversarial (L3, decision 0071 rulings 7 and 9). ledger.rs result_line guesses member boundaries from newlines. A continuation becomes a sibling bullet and can appear to carry another member’s verdict. A one-line, one-member panel appears inline, and multiline plain notes acquire extra bullets. The implementer chose this split to avoid a second shape reader. Preserve member boundaries through rendering and test one-member and multiline cases. The ledger is display-only.
Medium — correctness (L3, ruling 7). aggregate.rs records every verdict but only supplied notes. dashboard.rs panel_notes iterates only the notes map, so the ledger omits members who gave just a verdict and can print “no notes recorded” for the whole panel. Render these members in the ledger while preserving the L4 dashboard output.
Low — correctness (L1, ruling 5). notes_of and result_notes both look up /result/notes. Centralize the lookup while retaining the dashboard’s absence-only error fallback.
Low — correctness (ruling 9). The absent-notes golden pins the fallback, but the implementation evidence records no mutation that makes this new golden fail. Record the failure when changing the fallback text.
Verify reported a passing workspace suite and self-bundle compile. Exact coverage and the CRAP ratchet remain unverified.

Returned implement: this commit (731a40a5, on top of 9c53812a) answers all four review findings.
